meta.note: Thin day, six pieces. Seven strong items from this window already ran on 14 or 15 October and are not repeated (Pictoplasma, Pregnant Then Screwed, Milkshake, the CFO essay, Figma Specs, YouTube Music labels, the Adobe clones). Left out: Creative Bloq deals, reviews and game pieces, Nicer Tuesdays talk pages without text, artist portraits, member-only UX Collective essays (only openings readable), the Roastbrief run of hires and campaign releases, and the general TechCrunch, Ars Technica and MIT Technology Review tech news. The userresearchstrategist.com feed failed, six paid Substack posts were removed beforehand.

stories.title: Pohoda turns 30 with a typeface pulled from its own old posters
stories.blurb: For the festival’s third major identity, Andrej & Andrej redrew pre-2010 lettering from Pohoda’s own communications as a geometric, rounded display face. Its working trick: lowercase a, e and s share cap height and can snap to the top or bottom of the line, which lets artist names stack into tight blocks on the posters.

sources.name: It's Nice That
sources.headline: Andrej & Andrej gives Pohoda Festival an identity refresh, complete with 3D babies and a futuristic typeface

stories.title: Just Eat Takeaway moves from what it delivers to the time it gives back
stories.blurb: VCCP’s new global platform "Stay Just Where You Are" sits on one insight: people do not want to leave a good moment. The CMO frames it as a 20-year brief that keeps the "Did Somebody Say" mnemonic and existing assets while shifting the brand into emotional territory. The source is a press release, so the claims are the brand’s own.

sources.name: Roastbrief
sources.headline: Just Eat Takeaway.com says ‘Stay Just Where You Are’ with new global brand platform

stories.title: Karri Saarinen on why agent-built products start to feel like no one made them
stories.blurb: The Linear co-founder argues that products carry the point of view of their makers, and that additive changes shipped by individuals working with agents average that point of view away. His test is worth borrowing: a feature can work perfectly on its own and still make the product worse, and spotting that takes a belief about what the product should be.

stories.title: Deezer will let listeners switch off AI-generated music entirely
stories.blurb: A toggle due before year end removes AI tracks, albums and related artists from search. Deezer’s numbers explain why: more than half of daily uploads were AI-generated by July, about 90,000 tracks a day, and around 45% of customers asked for a filter. It is the strictest platform stance next to Bandcamp’s outright ban.

sources.name: TechCrunch
sources.headline: Deezer will soon let you filter out AI-generated music

stories.title: Cinema 4D 2027 finally gets a native scatter system
stories.blurb: Maxon’s 2027.0 release adds a Scatter Generator and Scatter Tag for populating scenes with vegetation, debris or crowds, driven by the familiar MoGraph Fields and Effectors. That closes a gap that used to push artists to third-party plugins. Liquid FX for foam and spray arrives in the same update.

sources.name: Creative Bloq
sources.headline: Cinema 4D finally gets one of the most-requested features in new 2027 release

stories.title: FLUX.3 Image Klein brings 4K generation and editing to an 8 GB GPU
stories.blurb: Black Forest Labs’ new open-weights image model has 5.6 billion parameters, generates natively in 4K, edits with up to ten reference images and is available in Diffusers and ComfyUI. Commercial use is free under the FLUX licence for companies below five million dollars in annual revenue.

sources.name: Hugging Face
sources.headline: Welcome FLUX.3 Image Klein in Diffusers
